title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Monday morning, Nov 16
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 7:30 AM ET Monday, Nov 16, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). Three new frames moved overnight. A Texas state senator's Freedman's Bureau bill became a national 'reparations ID cards' story (4,142 posts in 24 hours, 3.30× its prior daily average; 'Reparations' was on the U.S. trends list this morning). Rep.-elect Melat Kiros joined the 'earn my vote' bloc on Hakeem Jeffries (1,426 posts, 4.39×). And 'Texas Democrats are coming for your guns' spread on a list of about 25 prefiled bills that Snopes confirms exist, though none is close to law. Slotkin's 'Trump-proof' plan kept the 'CIA asset' frame running (2,904 posts, 4.81×), and the WSJ tax story is still rising three days in. Van Hollen vs. Schumer is still the largest conversation (29,441 posts). The FAA story, USAID, and the 'Seditious Six' are cooling. We added a direct 'rigged midterms' query: it's large (9,249 posts) but falling, and fact-checkers have rebutted its main claims. Every count, quote, and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this morning or carried over and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

trends.detail: U.S. trends were pulled at about 7:17 AM ET with x.get_trends_by_woeid (WOEID 23424977, max 50; 37 returned). Sunday Night Football (Bengals–Steelers), 'Good Monday,' music, and K-pop dominated. 'Reparations' was the only trend that matched a narrative we scored. X News's 'Reparations' results this morning were led by the Texas Freedman's Bureau bill, so the reparations card received the trend bonus; we did not verify which posts drove the trend itself. We requested tweet_count, but the trend objects did not include it, so trend volumes are unavailable and we did not estimate them.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. Several stories this morning are worked by both sides. The Right amplifies Melat Kiros, Don Leonard, and the NYC-DSA vote as a 'Democratic civil war,' and the Pressley draft overlaps with the reparations story through her H.R. 40 agenda. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Monday, Nov 16, 2026, 7:30 AM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 7:17 AM ET. Last night's snapshot (Nov 15, 5:30 PM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Eleven of its thirteen narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps last night's by 10 hours (7 AM to 5 PM ET Sunday), so read changes as a trend, not as independent days. Two narratives were dropped because they faded: the SAVE Act filibuster fight (2,415 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.17× its prior daily average) and Medicare for All as a leadership test (1,785, 0.50×), whose demands now appear in the Kiros and Pressley cards. Five narratives were added with new queries: the Texas reparations bureau bill, Melat Kiros, Texas gun bills, 'Make America Nice Again,' and a direct 'rigged midterms' query. Two other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: the Alaska Senate 'cheating' claim (665 posts, falling), which is covered in the rigged-midterms card, and protesters interrupting Jeffries in Denver (577 posts, 0.27×).

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity. We counted matches in a window from 7:00 AM ET Sunday, Nov 15, through 7:00 AM ET Monday, Nov 16 (exactly 24 hours). We also counted a 167-hour 'seven-day' window from 8:00 AM ET Monday, Nov 9 (the earliest whole-hour start the recent-count API allowed at pull time) to the same end point. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved in this morning's searches and cite on the card. Official government pages, bill text, advocacy groups, bill trackers, X News summaries, and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets. Sources carried over from earlier snapshots without being re-retrieved are not counted. We noted whether each topic appeared on the U.S. trends list at about 7:17 AM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list this morning. Score changes since last night reflect both volume and how much coverage we retrieved, so read the post counts alongside the scores. 'Make America Nice Again' had a near-zero baseline, so its acceleration index maxes out on 303 posts.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The filibuster query excludes SAVE Act posts, the Slotkin query excludes 'seditious,' the Leonard query includes the bare name 'Leonard' (every post in our samples was about Don Leonard), and the rigged-midterms query also catches posts mocking fraud claims. Replies are included, and automated @grok replies make up a visible share of several queries. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. The Electoral College, NYC-DSA, filibuster, and Seditious Six cards did not get a fresh sample this morning, and they say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatBody: New this morning: 'Texas Democrats filed a bill for reparations ID cards' is based on a real bill, SB 376. But posts claiming it pays reparations or traces 'all state residents' are missing context. The bill funds a bureau that helps people who choose to document freedmen ancestry and file claims, and a 2025 version died in committee. 'Texas Democrats filed about 20 gun bills' is true, per Snopes (25 firearm-related bills, including some by Republicans), but none has had a hearing, and Republicans hold the Texas Senate. Midterm 'rigged election' claims are fading but still large. Snopes found no proof Texas 'found' 20 million votes, and AFP traced an Ohio county's inflated totals to leftover mock-election data. In Alaska, the 'decoy Dan Sullivan' dispute is a real controversy, but it is not evidence of national fraud. Carried over: the FAA still says it has 'no indication' Friday's ground stop was a cyberattack. 'Slotkin is a CIA asset running a color revolution' remains unsupported. The 'Seditious Six' money-laundering rumor remains unverified, and a grand jury declined to indict the six in February. Pressley has still not launched a speaker bid. 'Democrats want to restore USAID' still lacks a bill.

narratives.title: NEW: 'Reparations ID cards' — a Texas Freedman's Bureau bill becomes a national 'Democrats want reparations' story
narratives.query: (reparations OR "H.R. 40" OR "HR 40" OR "Freedmen's Bureau" OR "Freedman's Bureau") (Democrats OR Democrat OR Dems OR Pressley OR Texas OR "Borris Miles" OR Congress) lang:en
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM ET Sunday to 7 AM ET Monday, most top matches were near-identical copies of one template ('WTF? A Texas Democrat just filed a bill to create REPARATIONS ID CARDS'), plus 'taxpayer-funded race-based' framing and questions about equal protection. Automated @grok replies were a visible share of matches; most confirmed the bill exists and described it as a database people would opt into. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: The top-scoring narrative this morning: 4,142 posts in the last 24 hours, 3.30 times its prior daily average, and 'Reparations' was on the U.S. X trends list at about 7:17 AM ET. Volume jumped from 50 to 164 and then 320 posts an hour starting at 10 AM ET Sunday. That followed a 9:47 AM ET post from @GuntherEagleman: 'A Texas Democrat just filed a bill to create REPARATIONS ID CARDS' (2,883 likes, 1,765 reposts, 69,275 views). Copy-paste versions followed all day, and the biggest peak came at 7 and 8 PM ET (492 and 410 posts). The bill is real. Texas SB 376, prefiled Nov. 13 by state Sen. Borris Miles (D-Houston), would create a 'Texas Freedman's Bureau' under the Health and Human Services Commission, run by five commissioners the governor appoints. It would keep a database to help residents establish ancestral ties to people freed from slavery between 1861 and 1868, give a 'freedmen identification card' to residents who establish those ties, and 'assist residents who are descendants of freedmen with obtaining reparations, including by providing legal assistance with filing claims.' The bill would not pay reparations itself. A bill-tracking site notes it repeats the text of SB 2918, which died in committee in 2025, and Republicans still control the Texas Senate. X News also summarized Rep. Ayanna Pressley's posted agenda for the new majority, which includes reparations through H.R. 40.
talkingPoints: Democrats won Texas for five minutes and they're already handing out reparations ID cards.
A race-based state ancestry database: what could go wrong?
Taxpayers will fund lawyers to help people sue taxpayers.
This is what 'affordability' meant all along.
narratives.amplifiers: Named accounts in posts we opened: @GuntherEagleman (2,883 likes, 1,765 reposts, 69,275 views); @JohnBasham ('TAXPAYER-FUNDED RACE-BASED FREEDMEN ID CARDS,' 317 likes, 204 reposts, 49,147 views); @MamaInfosaurus (47 likes, 1,138 views); and dozens of copy-paste accounts. X News clustered the story late Sunday.
narratives.whyItWorks: It packs race, taxes, and government databases into one image: an ID card. It also lets the Right nationalize one state senator's bill as the plan of the new Democratic majority, and the label 'reparations' does the work before anyone reads the text.
narratives.audience: Conservative and MAGA-aligned voters, Texans uneasy about the Democratic sweep, and white working-class swing voters who respond to 'race-based' framing.
narratives.counter: Read the bill. SB 376 sets up a bureau to help people who choose to trace freedmen ancestry and file claims. It appropriates no reparations payments, and the same text died in committee last session. It still has to clear a Republican Texas Senate. If the topic comes up, separate a symbolic state bill from any federal program. H.R. 40, the federal bill, would create a study commission, not payments.

factChecks.claim: Texas Democrats filed a bill to pay reparations and build a genealogy database of all state residents.
factChecks.detail: SB 376's text creates a bureau that maintains a database 'for the purpose of assisting residents of this state in establishing ancestral ties with freedmen,' issues ID cards to residents who establish those ties, and provides legal help filing reparations claims. It does not appropriate reparations payments or require every resident to be traced. The bill is prefiled, not passed, and a 2025 version died in committee. This is TDDR's read of the bill text, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

narratives.title: 'Slotkin is a CIA asset running a color revolution' — now riding her 'Trump-proof the government' pitch
narratives.query: Slotkin ("CIA asset" OR "color revolution" OR reimagine OR reimagining OR "Trump proof" OR "Trump-proof" OR "after Trump") -seditious lang:en
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM ET Sunday to 7 AM ET Monday, the top posts paired 'Trump proof' with 'rigging the system' and 'brazen corruption,' and the 'CIA asset… Color Revolution to destroy the USA' post kept circulating. A separate set of near-identical pro-Slotkin template posts ('In a powerful moment, Senator Elissa Slotkin just laid out how Democrats are going to "Trump proof" the government') pushed the other way. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: Holding its pace: 2,904 posts in the last 24 hours, about level with the 2,978 in last night's window (the two windows overlap by 10 hours), and 4.81 times its prior daily average. Its score is 77, the same as last night. Volume held between about 115 and 195 posts an hour from 7 AM ET Sunday into the evening, then eased overnight. The frame is shifting. This morning's top matches are less about the Carnegie 'reimagine' clip and more about Slotkin's pledge to 'Trump proof' the government. Steve Gruber's post — 'Slotkin just unveiled the Democrats' plan to "Trump proof" the government… They're rigging the system' — drew 1,403 likes, 723 reposts, and 30,945 views. Vox describes the plan she has pitched for a Democratic majority in three parts: housing and health-care bills, accountability in 'signature cases' of alleged misuse of taxpayer money and power, and reforms so no future president can exploit the same weaknesses. The 'CIA asset' and 'color revolution' labels still ride along in replies. Slotkin is also one of the 'Seditious Six,' which keeps the two Right-wing cards linked.
talkingPoints: Slotkin is ex-CIA, and there's no such thing as ex-CIA.
'Reimagine the systems' means tear up the Constitution.
This is the color-revolution playbook from Eastern Europe, now on American soil.
She went to Hungary and Poland to learn how to take down a government.
narratives.amplifiers: Named accounts in posts we opened: @stevegrubershow (1,403 likes, 723 reposts, 30,945 views); @Keltic_Spirit, 'Elissa Slotkin is a CIA asset' (272 likes, 161 reposts, 3,326 views); @BrettDoyleMCS ('went to Hungary on an exercise of Color Revolution'); and pro-Slotkin template accounts such as @Alexwestlivee.
narratives.whyItWorks: It fuses a true biographical fact (she worked at the CIA) with a vague quote ('build something new') and an existing Right-wing frame ('color revolution'). Listeners can fill a vague quote with their worst fears, and the biography makes the conspiracy feel like evidence.
narratives.audience: MAGA-aligned and conspiracy-curious audiences, Trump supporters primed by the 'Seditious Six' posts, and some anti-establishment voters on the left who distrust the intelligence agencies.
narratives.counter: Play the tape; don't paraphrase it. The Carnegie event was about broad coalitions, anti-corruption cases, and free elections, the same tools the Right praised when they were used against governments it opposed. Don't defend vague language, either. Ask Slotkin to name the 'systems' she means.

factChecks.claim: Slotkin's call to 'reimagine and build something new' after Trump is a CIA-run 'color revolution' plan to overthrow the government.
factChecks.detail: The remarks appear to come from a public Carnegie Endowment event billed as lessons from Hungary and Poland on defending democracy. Her office's summary describes building coalitions, exposing corruption, and protecting free elections. Posts making the 'CIA asset' claim offered no evidence beyond her past CIA employment. We found no fact-check outlet rating the claim; this is TDDR's read of the event record and the coverage we retrieved.

The first '7 AM' bar is Sunday; the last '6 AM' bar is Monday. Volume held steady from Sunday morning into the evening and eased overnight. That points to a broad, reply-driven narrative rather than one viral post. The query excludes 'seditious' to limit overlap with the Seditious Six card.
